To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal privacy level, subscription fee, bundling profit, and profit sharing among the interrelated services are all functions of the degree of contingency, i.e., the correlation between the interrelated data.

1) the optimal privacy level for a standalone service decreases with the service quality, 2) the optimal privacy levels for complementary and substitute services increase and decrease with the service quality of the other services, respectively, 3) the profit of service bundling increases with the degree of complementarity and decreases with the degree of substitutability, and 4) the profit sharing ratio between the cooperative providers is proportional to the market value of the bundle and the market value of their own service.

(i) the optimal privacy management and pricing of people-centric sensing data depend on the service quality, (ii) the service providers should cooperate to sell complementary services, and (iii) the profit sharing among the service providers should be fair and proportional to their contributions to the bundling profit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
privacy management and profit sharing for interrelated people-centric sensing services.
the pricing and bundling strategies for people-centric sensing services.
the pricing and bundling of services in people-centric sensing and the privacy management of people-centric data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal privacy management and pricing of interrelated people-centric sensing services can be achieved through the cooperation of service bundling and profit sharing.
the optimal pricing, service bundling, and profit sharing of interrelated people-centric service can be achieved by the proposed models.
the optimal service pricing is correlated with the privacy level and the degree of contingency among services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the privacy and pricing of interrelated people-centric data are jointly optimized to maximize the profit of the service providers and to maximize the social welfare.
people-centric services can be sold with the optimal privacy level to maximize profit.
the optimal pricing of interrelated people-centric data is correlated with the privacy level, and service bundling is profitable for complementary services but detrimental for substitutes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal pricing and privacy level are dependent on the service type and interrelationship.
people-centric sensing can provide a better understanding of the interplay between the optimal privacy level, pricing, and bunding of people-centric services.
the optimal privacy level, pricing, and bundlement of people-centric services should be carefully designed and managed to maximize the service providers' profits.
